clue.text: Fireworks, which once lit ancient evenings?

blocks.note: the plain sense: a kind of firework that shoots out coloured balls
the playful sense: candles that people in ancient Rome would have burned after dark

explanation.surface: Someone muses on how fireworks might once have brightened the nights of the ancient world.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: read literally, the firework's name describes the candles of an ancient Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the established name for a tube-shaped firework that fires a series of glowing balls.

clue.text: Withdrawal of me or Val, perhaps

indicators.note: 'perhaps' suggests the letters could be arranged some other way than shown

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which of two people, themselves or a friend called Val, will pull out.
explanation.definitionFit: A taking away or pulling out of something is a removal, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Put Frenchman on before long rainy season

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur
taken as written
before long means shortly

explanation.surface: An instruction to send a Frenchman onstage before a lengthy wet spell.
explanation.walkthrough: M for Monsieur is a standard crossword abbreviation for a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: The season of heavy rain brought by seasonal winds in South Asia is called by this name.

clue.text: Unusually cold rains over southern States produce spring flower

indicators.note: something done unusually is done in an odd way, so these letters come out in an odd order

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for southern
the United States

explanation.surface: A weather report: freak cold rain over the southern US brings out the spring blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the reworked letters above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The genus that includes daffodils and the poet's narcissus flowers in spring.

clue.text: Strange Channel Islands tat found in loft

indicators.note: something strange is out of its normal shape, so the letters are put in an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands
taken as written

explanation.surface: Odd junk from Jersey or Guernsey turns up stored in someone's loft.
explanation.walkthrough: Tat is British slang for cheap junk; the Channel Islands are British islands off Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: The roof space at the top of a house is called either word, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Fibber floored by Spooner in local language

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of neighbouring words, so this asks for that swap

blocks.note: a fibber is a liar, and someone floored has been knocked down

explanation.surface: A liar is knocked to the ground by the Oxford don famous for his verbal slips.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the L and D sounds at the start of the two words and you get something close to 'dier lecked'.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional variety of a language, with its own words and grammar, is a dialect.

clue.text: Stimulate even nil variety

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so these letters are made into a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Livening up a drab scoreless draw by mixing things around.
explanation.definitionFit: To liven up or excite something is to stimulate it, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Converned with good eating, without beginning to become extremely large

indicators.note: having no beginning means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: relating to fine food and the art of eating well

explanation.surface: A food lover's interest grows until it becomes enormous, much like a waistline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converned' is the source's typo for 'Concerned'. Dropping the G from the start of the food word leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures as vast as the distances between stars are informally called astronomical, meaning huge.

clue.text: Half ran back to reach discussion group

indicators.note: going back means the word ran is written from its end to its start

blocks.note: semi- is the prefix meaning half
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner covers half the distance before turning round to join a study group.
explanation.definitionFit: A small class meeting to discuss a subject with a tutor is a seminar.

clue.text: Film extract shows chase on East River

blocks.note: to chase is to trail or follow
E is the abbreviation for East
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A movie clip features a pursuit along the bank of an eastern river.
explanation.definitionFit: A short preview made of clips from a forthcoming movie, used to advertise it in cinemas.

clue.text: Queen in posh car to overtake King - one on little wheels

indicators.note: the monarch sits inside the vehicle, so one piece goes inside the other
'over' is read loosely here as turned over, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a Rolls-Royce, the classic luxury car
ER, Elizabeth Regina
split as over plus take; the second half is used as written
R, Rex

explanation.surface: The Queen, chauffeured in her limousine, tries to pass the King on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is loose: the last five letters are a jumble of 'take' with R for King, signalled only by 'over'. ER and R are the royal Latin abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A person moving on boots fitted with small wheels is a skater of that kind.

clue.text: Rosemary topping Olivia concocted for pasta dish

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, which sits above the rest
something concocted is mixed up from ingredients, so the name's letters are mixed

blocks.note: the opening letter of the herb
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Olivia cooks a pasta dish garnished with a sprig of rosemary.
explanation.definitionFit: Small square pasta parcels with a filling, served as a dish, go by this Italian name.

clue.text: Aromatic herb served cold with her very Italian lasagne starters

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold
taken as written
the first letters of three words

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a fragrant herb goes on her cold Italian lasagne as a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicate aniseed-scented herb related to parsley, used in French cooking, is chervil.

clue.text: Only new mixture is used for synthetic material

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A fabric label claims only a fresh blend goes into making man-made cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a man-made polymer fibre, the archetypal artificial fabric.

clue.text: Take coach up to St Anne's partly on church matter

indicators.note: in an across answer 'up' is read as going back, so the word is written backwards
only part of the saint's name is used, so its tail is cut off

blocks.note: a coach is a kind of bus
taken letter for letter
CE, the Church of England

explanation.surface: Travel directions: catch a coach up to St Anne's, a place by the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical material of a particular kind is called a substance, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Note single feature first in porcelain

blocks.note: B is one of the musical notes
single means one
a facial feature
A is the first letter, or a first-class grade

explanation.surface: An observation about the one standout feature of a piece of fine porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' means part of the face here, not a distinguishing quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine white English porcelain made with bone ash is the type named here.

clue.text: Medical Officer with regiment meeting Stalin changed into something unforgivable

indicators.note: the dictator's name is changed, meaning its letters are put in another order

blocks.note: MO is the abbreviation for Medical Officer
R is the abbreviation for regiment
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An army doctor and his regiment meet the Soviet dictator and are transformed into something beyond pardon.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic teaching a grave sin that cuts the soul off from grace, deemed past forgiving without repentance.

clue.text: She (the first Mrs de Winter) is about to be 100 (approximately)

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for 100
ca. is short for circa, meaning approximately

explanation.surface: A woman from a famous novel is said to be nearing her hundredth birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: In Daphne du Maurier's novel the narrator is the second Mrs de Winter; the dead first wife gives the book its title.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the du Maurier novel is Maxim de Winter's first wife.

clue.text: Used caution at sale

indicators.note: something used is worked over and handled, so the letters come out in a different order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A careful buyer kept their wits about them while bidding at the saleroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A public sale where goods go to whoever bids the highest price is this kind of sale.

clue.text: Stitch up with silver in pay packet

indicators.note: 'up' in an across answer means turned backwards, so the word is written from the end
'with' here means holding, so the metal is placed inside the other word

blocks.note: to stitch is to sew
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone is framed or cheated, with silver coins hidden in their pay envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitch up' reads as the British slang for framing someone, but it splits into the verb and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pay packet is the envelope of weekly earnings, so it stands for the money paid.

clue.text: Shaped with hard time

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
hard as in tough or harsh
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something formed through tough times, as a character is shaped by hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: The old past participle of work, as in wrought iron, means formed or fashioned.

clue.text: Picked up article on injured leg by journalist

indicators.note: something injured is knocked out of shape, so the limb's letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
an indefinite article
ED, an editor

explanation.surface: A reporter writes up a story about a damaged leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' puts the article below the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather bit by bit, as gleaners picked up grain left after harvest.

clue.text: Little boy scout's in charge of empty lakeside kiosk

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: a Cub is a junior member of the Scouts
IC means in charge
the first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A young scout is put in charge of a hut beside the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A small booth or enclosed compartment, like a kiosk, is a cubicle.

clue.text: Land's short shortage

indicators.note: being short means a letter is missing, here from the front

blocks.note: a dearth is a lack

explanation.surface: A complaint that there is a scarcity of land.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'short' is the signal and the second is part of the word to shorten; dropping the D leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth means the ground or dry land as opposed to sea, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Water losing one H atom (in clear error) will cause disease

indicators.note: losing one atom of hydrogen means one of the two H symbols is taken away
placed in means the shortened formula goes inside the other letters
something in error has gone wrong, so the letters are in the wrong order

blocks.note: the formula for water is H2O, two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A chemistry warning: bad water caused by a mistake will spread disease.
explanation.walkthrough: H2O minus one H leaves HO, which sits inside a reordering of the word clear.
explanation.definitionFit: An infectious bacterial illness of the intestines, spread by contaminated drinking water.

clue.text: Carry UK relic around to bring better fortune

indicators.note: moving letters around shifts them into a different order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone carries a British relic about with them like a lucky charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Being more fortunate, enjoying more good luck than others, is the comparative meaning here.

clue.text: Naive girl is awfully genuine

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An innocent young woman is described as terribly sincere.
explanation.definitionFit: An innocent, unsophisticated young woman, especially as a stock stage role, is an ingenue.

clue.text: Inclusion of sofa in the Art Edition is lacking in boldness

indicators.note: something included is contained within the words that follow, running across them

blocks.note: letters running from the end of the furniture word to the start of the last word

explanation.surface: A timid design magazine features a sofa in its art issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone timid and without courage is described as faint-hearted, a lack of nerve.
